newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Australia's RGC sees Ukraine gold deal failing.
newsitem.headline: Australia's RGC sees Ukraine gold deal failing.

text.p: A multi-million dollar deal between Ukraine and Australia's RGC to develop gold deposits looks likely to fall through after they failed to reach a deal forming a joint venture, an RGC spokesman said on Friday.
"Our view is the project is dead," John Elder, manager of the RGC representative office in Kiev, told Reuters.
Elder said RGC and the Industry Ministry signed a memorandum last year to form a joint venture by early June.
However, before signing, RGC wanted clarification of legal matters such as privatisation of state assets.
"The ministry informed us that since the deadline is passed it was looking to involve other companies," Elder said.
"In RGC's view the deposit was marginal but still we would have continued evaluating and forming a joint-venture if given the necessary time and necessary legal guarantees."

He also indicated that the company might now pull out of Ukraine altogether, saying, "RGC is certainly evaluating its options in Ukraine right now. We've spent a lot of money on our Ukrainian programme."
No one was available to comment from the ministry, which last year announced a programme to develop a gold industry by 2001 and had put RGC's potential investment at $30 million.

Government ministers have promised to improve the investment climate in Ukraine in recent months after U.S. communications giant Motorola pulled out of a GSM licensing project potentially worth millions of dollars earlier this year. Foreign investors and countries have criticised Ukraine for inconsistent and changing laws, high taxes and corruption.
"Ukraine, in terms of investment legislation, mining legislation and bureaucracy is probably at the bottom of the list in terms of attractiveness for companies," Elder said.
Elder said the company had spent $1 million on the gold project and had given the government a $250,000 "good faith payment" to cover costs of the existing Myzhiyevsky operation.
"A full feasibility study was not completed but a large-scale facility like that could have been worth $100 million. It was possible," he said.
He added RGC had spent $1 million on a project in 1995 to evaluate a tailings deposit for titanium and zircon in western Ukraine's Zhytomyr region but was later turned down by the government.
